x: Johnny Johnson, our "guest" member from Sheffield, was another who turned up on October 6th. It speaks well for his enthusiasm, as apparently he only docked at Tilbury early in the morning, and had come practically straight along to Belgrave Hall to give us his greetings personally.
Johnny Johnson, our Sheffield member, is now demobbed. He has been doing some good publicity for the Club by showing the magazine to his Northern friends.

Newcomer from Ireland John Johnson failed to break 100 minutes but scored in the team. This cheerful addition to our ranks looks a good prospect for the longer distance teams when stamina counts for more than speed.

A warm up for the National team but also the chance for newcomer Johnny Johnson to break the hour for Six miles. His margin of 3½ minutes suggests that it will not be long before a 7 in the hour badge also comes his way.
…eat walkers could surely have pulled something out. A disappointing day for Belgrave although that vocal Irish newcomer John Johnson staged an entertaining finale to his first national.…
Those Belgrave landmarks John Keown, John Morris and George Beecham are still very much alive and will, one hopes shortly be joined by John Johnson.

The veterans of Belgrave, well versed in the ways of the Brighton road, stand quietly out of the way of brasher newcomers with less experience and more to say;John Keown and John Morris are joined this year by John Johnson and Wally Wortley.
Denis McKeown was 10th, Charlie Henn 14th, John Blair-Fish 20th, John V. Baker 24th, and John Johnson - playing hookey from the walking section - 26th.

A special presentation of an attache case (donated by J.Johnson) was made to Jack Goswell to commemorate his 21st 'Open' and with usual 'Goswell' efficiency, result sheets were circulated before the hall was closed.

Welcome appearances were made by Percy Wilson and John Johnson, both of whom have suffered serious problems during 1972.
